comparator.name: Bachelor in Management of International Social Challenges
comparator.sourceNotes: Adopted ESSB 2026–2027 EER Appendix III C p.39 and current public programme overview independently checked 20 October 2026: 23 components, three 60-EC years, compulsory 6.5-EC Designing Social Research, 7.5-EC year-2 Research Project, 15-EC year-3 minor and compulsory 15-EC Bachelor Project. Contrary to the earlier checkpoint, the current public overview now also lists Designing Social Research. Open minor space is preserved without inventing its content; approved exchange/internship possibilities remain choices, not additional credits. This v2 decision is a guarded recovery of an existing record whose earlier root decision was absent, not a replay of a historical decision. Enriched workbook blob c2bcc3b63ec7831fd0f7b8ddfb32de1260521655 supplies current course content, prerequisites and availability.

questions: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
Which development and migration strategies work, and under what governance conditions?
How should climate change be governed across public, private and societal actors?
How does technological change affect public organisations?

Introduction to Sociology provides the foundational sociological concepts needed to analyse social structures and institutions
directly studies public international law, including treaties, armed conflict, refugee law and environmental law; these are legal dimensions of cross-border social challenges

directly teaches qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and dissemination through a social research project

contributes complementary normative analysis of equality, poverty, future generations, climate change and historical injustice, supporting the evidenced distinction between normative judgments and empirical governance analysis

directly examines EU institutions, legal foundations, citizenship and free movement, enabling legal analysis of European governance alongside political study
directly teaches quantitative causal and predictive analysis using regression, instrumental variables, statistical tests and an empirical economic paper

examines social movements and environmental justice using environmental-conflict cases, contributing directly to the social mobilisation and inequality dimensions of international sustainability challenges
provides complementary environmental-system foundations through planetary boundaries and thresholds; these define physical constraints relevant to climate and sustainability governance

develops waves, materials and chemical foundations used to understand the physical requirements of low-carbon technologies. It contributes science that complements climate governance; it does not teach public policy or international administration

studies chemical and technological aspects of resource recovery and the circular economy. Its lab-based work complements sustainability-policy assessment, without substituting for social policy analysis

provides a sustainability research project with regional external partners; it contributes applied research on an evidenced challenge, without guaranteeing public-policy content or a compulsory thesis equivalent

applies technical and economic energy-system assessment to renewable transition decisions for a partner organisation; it provides a concrete intervention context complementary to public climate governance

candidates.label: A migration and global-development route centred on migration policy, development strategies, international law and multilevel governance.

A climate and sustainability governance route that uses the programme's explicit climate-change challenge as the organising question and combines environmental systems, governance, sociology, economics, law and communication.
A technology-and-public-organisations route focused on how technological change affects public organisations.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match and the climate/sustainability governance route are both defensible. The climate route is the strongest additional option because its evidence produces a genuine seven-course curricular shift. A migration/development candidate could not support a third alternative: the substitutions needed to cross the threshold did not implement migration or development and therefore failed qualitative distinctness. The technology-and-public-organisations interest was also assessed for completeness and found not feasible as a coherent 24-course route.

alternatives.label: Closest match to Management of International Social Challenges
alternatives.concept: Politics, international law, sociology, economics and organisational study are combined to examine how institutions and public actors respond to international social challenges. Qualitative and quantitative research support the analysis of governance and policy.
alternatives.labelReason: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and accurately presents this option as the closest feasible UCR response to Bachelor in Management of International Social Challenges, rather than as a narrower subfield.
progression: Passed. Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology and New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory; research-method and economics courses progress from foundations to advanced work, with formal prerequisites and term availability satisfied.

alternatives.label: Climate and sustainability governance
alternatives.concept: Climate and sustainability questions connect governance, economics, sociology, law and communication with environmental science and technology. The programme examines both collective decisions and the physical systems involved in sustainability transitions.
alternatives.labelReason: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and describes its substantive organising direction without treating the generating concept as an official UCR track or overstating one strand of the programme.
progression: Formal prerequisites and all six planned terms checked directly against the enriched workbook. Climate Change precedes Governance of Sustainability; the latter has no formal prerequisite and introduces governance concepts, so semester-2 placement is defensible. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and the dependent 300-level technical courses; Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology and contemporary social theory. Early 300-level status alone is not a progression defect.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces seven courses (52.5 EC) with environmental systems, sustainability governance, circular-resource study, renewable-system design, applied sustainability research and public communication. Those changes follow directly from the evidenced climate-change and Sustainable Development Goals direction.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme combines a structured Public Administration curriculum with international law, migration, development, research methods and a bachelor project. UCR can assemble strong multidisciplinary programmes around global governance and specific international challenges, but does not reproduce the same dedicated MISOC sequence or its named International Migration and Global Development Issues courses.

audience.programmeDescription: Management of International Social Challenges at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how public organisations address problems across national borders, including migration, global development, climate change and economic instability. Students study politics, policy, international law, sociology, economics and management alongside social research and a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines substantial governance, international law, political, social, economic, organisational and research study. A second option focuses on climate and sustainability governance, including complementary environmental science and technology. These are related UCR programmes rather than equivalents to Erasmus’s dedicated MISOC curriculum; the specialist migration and development courses, policy-analysis sequence and required 15-EC bachelor project remain gaps.
